objections.claim: The spec's containment argument rests entirely on tier routing (`resolveVerificationTier` ignores class for non-DONE sources), but `classifyCriterion`'s class label is itself a consumed output with its own routing semantics. `cmdDod`'s own docstring in the supplied file states the classifier exists "for the evaluator to decide which it may machine-judge (scenario/assertion) vs force to needs-human (prose)." A Scenarios unit whose only `<`/`>` is a placeholder — e.g. "Then `faff state <issue>` resolves an issue's local state" — currently classifies `assertion` and is machine-judgeable by the code-blind holdout (which can absolutely exercise a CLI verb). After the change it classifies `prose`, and the evaluator forces it to `needs-human`. The spec's claim "The class label on a Scenarios unit therefore changes no verifier. Only DONE items move" is wrong: the verifier (tier) is unchanged, but the *judged set* shrinks, in the exact misroute direction the ticket exists to fix — items leave the holdout that the holdout could observe.
objections.evidence: `plugin/skills/faff/bin/lib/admissibility.js`, `cmdDod` docstring ("which it may machine-judge (scenario/assertion) vs force to needs-human (prose)"); spec §3 "Routing is unchanged for Scenarios units" and §2 "Scenarios-unit *routing* is not re-opened."
objections.predicted_consequence: The first placeholder-bearing Scenarios unit in a committed spec is punted `needs-human` by the evaluator despite being holdout-observable, contradicting the spec's own "Only DONE items move" and shrinking the judged set the FAFF-1270 goal depends on; the before/after measurement in the DONE section (which counts only DONE items) will not even detect it.

objections.claim: The mask `<[A-Za-z0-9-]+>` fires on any fully-bracketed alphanumeric token, and the text it masks is written by the same producer agent whose delivered feature the holdout later judges — an actor this system explicitly distrusts (spawner-attestation ratchets, code-blind evaluation, "a hand-authored `met` can never reach a record through this path"). Any real comparison written with a closing bracket — "p99 latency MUST be <200ms>", "requests <1000>/s", "retries <3>" — matches the mask in full (`200ms`, `1000`, `3` are all inside `[A-Za-z0-9-]+`), leaves no surviving operator, classifies `prose`, and routes `delegated` to the AC checklist, which is filled by the build's own reviewer. The item silently leaves the judged set; the holdout can return `meets-spec` on the remainder and the merge gate opens with the regression never exercised code-blind. The spec's stated bounds — the tight charset, "requires a closing `>` so no operator fragment is ever masked" — are precisely the shape the spec author controls, and the historical measurement over committed specs constrains past authors, not a future one. The design also adds no advisory, flag, or output marker when the mask fires, so the move is invisible to every downstream audit. This is a fail-open path in the merge gate the design creates, not a careless-build risk.
objections.evidence: §The placeholder shape ("an opening `<`, one or more letters/digits/hyphens, a closing `>`, with nothing else between the brackets"); §Failure modes ("A mis-masked real comparison would silently leave the holdout … the tight `<[A-Za-z0-9-]+>` shape (requires a closing bracket) is what bounds this"); §6-design-decision-rationale ("the mask hits no real comparison in committed specs" — a backward-looking control offered as the bound).
objections.predicted_consequence: a real threshold or behavioural assertion is dropped from the holdout's judged set with no signal; the holdout returns `meets-spec`; the merge gate passes with the regression verified only by the build's own self-attested AC checklist.

objections.claim: The measurement DONE item's safety value rests on recording "the placeholder-only delta," but "placeholder-only" is identified using the very mask under test — a mis-masked real comparison is counted as placeholder-only by construction. The measurement is therefore circular: it reports the safe answer even when a real comparison was masked, so it cannot serve as the evidence that "no real comparison reclassified." The delta items must be classified by a mask-independent method (e.g. manual review of every moved item against the unmasked text) for the control to bite.
objections.evidence: §Measurement ("the before/after count of `assertion`-class DONE items and the placeholder-only delta are recorded"); §6-design-decision-rationale ("the mask hits no real comparison in committed specs; the crude-parser figure above is supporting evidence, not the gate").
objections.predicted_consequence: the gate the spec relies on to prove the mask safe confirms safety even when a real comparison left the holdout.
